thread:
maria: Heads-up: dashboard sparklines are showing 3-4s render stalls in canary after last bundle roll (widgets chunk + telemetry proxy landed). Traces point to heavy parse/exec on main thread.
ryan: Ugh. Is that the EU canary or global?
sophie: saw a small LCP blip on staging too, but thought it was noise. Do we have a flamegraph? :eyes:
maria: EU canary only so far (rollout id r-2026-03-20-18). Quick flame: main.js -> telemetry-init -> chart-widget -> parseLargeDataset. Attached snippet: ```flame: main.js:telemetry-init:45ms -> chart-widget:320ms -> parseLargeDataset:1200ms```
jordan: Could be the new kv-prefetch change from routing policy PR #3298. We increased prefetch window and bumped max-concurrency for prefetch. If kvcache responses are larger, they trigger more parsing.
ryan: That PR also tweaked chunk-splitting so plots fetch bigger vectors. Are we double-parsing? Maybe telemetry client is hydrating then chart lib re-parses JSON.
maria: Repro steps: on EU canary user with >1k datapoints in a series, open dashboard -> click timeframe -> observe 3-4s jank. Console shows two parse XHRs: /api/v1/metrics?s=...&format=json (460KB) then /api/v1/metrics?downsample=true (420KB). Both parsed sequentially.
sophie: Can we short-circuit telemetry-init on canary? It looks like telemetry eager-init happens before worker fallback. If telemetry imports before worker bootstrap, everything parses on main thread. Maybe a conditional import will help.
jordan: Quick experiment: flip ROUTING_PREFETCH_WINDOW from 30s -> 5s and set PREFETCH_MAX_ITEMS=200 in canary config. That reduces payloads — might avoid duplicate JSON loads.
maria: I pushed a patch to the canary config (r-2026-03-20-18-config) to reduce prefetch window. Deploy bot says: deploy-bot: rollout r-2026-03-20-18-config started -> stage: canary -> id: dpl-6055551240.
ryan: Nice. Also can we change chart lib to accept NDJSON stream so we can parse incrementally? Longer-term, but could save 500-800ms on big series.
sophie: Short-term: lazy-init telemetry until worker is ready. I can open a tiny PR with dynamic import around telemetry client. Should be low-risk.
jordan: Also check bundle sizes: the new telemetry proxy added ~18KB gz but pulled in a polyfill that added 90KB. That could explain main thread bloat. We should prune polyfill or load it conditionally.
maria: After config flip + canary redeploy, EU canary shows median render from 3.8s -> 720ms on my quick sample. Still seeing edge cases at 1.2s for very wide series.
ryan: Great improvement. Keep the canary for a few hours and then decide rollback vs progressive rollout. Also add a telemetry event to gate and measure user-visible jank.
sophie: I'll send a small telemetry event name: "dashboard.render.jank" with buckets for render_ms. Want me to attach to the canary flag?
maria: Yes — add it to r-2026-03-20-18. Also log whether parse happened on main thread or worker.
jordan: Filed follow-ups: #3301 (chart ndjson streaming), #3302 (telemetry lazy-init), #3303 (polyfill audit).
maria: Thanks all. Will monitor canary for 4h and report back. :thumbsup:
